definition: Something or someone that a person or group strongly dislikes or completely rejects.
example: Wasting food was anathema to my grandmother, who saved every vegetable scrap for soup.
nuance: A bane causes trouble, but an anathema is rejected on principle because it goes against someone's deepest values.
prompt: A librarian who values quiet sets the rules for the reading room.
options: Loud phone calls were anathema to the librarian, who prized silence.
The librarian adored quiet, so a silent study hall was anathema to her.
The librarian softly hummed a cheerful anathema while she shelved new novels.
Free earplugs proved an anathema that cured the noise problem for good.
reasons: Noisy calls clash with everything she values, so she rejects them firmly.
This reverses the meaning: a thing she loves cannot be what she detests.
This confuses the word with the look-alike anthem; it is not a song.
A cure-all is a panacea; the word names something hated, not a remedy.

practice.prompt: A chef known for cooking only with fresh ingredients plans her menu.
options: The chef loved fresh herbs so dearly that they were anathema to her cooking.
The chef's anathema was the warm stew that guests requested at every holiday dinner.
The chef told a funny anathema about her first burned soufflé.
Canned vegetables were anathema to the chef, who shopped for produce daily.
reasons: Something she treasures cannot also be the thing she rejects.
A beloved signature dish is a favorite, not an object of loathing.
A short amusing story is an anecdote; the word does not mean a tale.
Canned food goes against her commitment to freshness, so she shuns it.
